Think of a heatmap like a scatter plot for categorical data.
In fact, we’ve seen how a scatter plot can be converted into a heatmap with the Matplotlib’s
. Heatmaps can almost always be used to show the distribution of values in a wide table. As such, they are a good compliment to subplots generated from such tables.
Seeing structure in a large table at a glance.
The advantage of a heatmap is that it shows
: blocks, stripes and criss-crosses, and gaps jump out that you would never notice scanning raw numbers.
A square matrix of relationships between variables (or predicted-vs-actual class counts) is often  shown as a heatmap.
A heatmap can be used to show the pair-wise, co-ocurrence data. They are a good compliment to network diagrams of the same data.
Let’s create a heatmap from scratch.
We’ll use a dataset of passenger counts on airline flights grouped by year and month.
This gives us a table of two grouping variables and a measurement one.
